transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me today. Um, well, I hope I'm not making a mountain out of a molehill, but... I guess I've been having a little trouble with forgetting things lately. 

Things I really shouldn't be slipping up on, to be honest. Like, uh, I keep missing my heart follow-up appointments, or I'll completely forget to call the clinic back when I'm supposed to. And even with everyday things, like if I set out to do a little repair job around the house, I'll show up to do it and realize I didn't bring the right tools with me. 

It's a bit embarrassing to admit, really, because I always try my best to keep on top of things. Is that... does that make sense? I hope I'm in the right place and not wasting your time with all this.
Have you had this kind of forgetfulness or trouble staying organized since childhood?

Well, gosh... yes, I suppose it goes back quite a ways. To be perfectly honest, even as a boy in grade school, I was... well, I guess you could say I was a very spirited kid. Not that I ever meant to cause trouble! I just had a bit too much energy, I think. 

I was always the kid who couldn't ever seem to stay in his seat. And I'd get so eager to participate that I'd just blurt out the answers before the teacher even finished asking or called on me. I actually... well, it's a little embarrassing to admit, but I used to get notes sent home to my parents because I talked a bit too much in class. I always felt terrible about it because I really did want to be a good student and make my teachers happy. 

Is that... I hope that's the kind of thing you're asking about? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information, Doctor.
